headline: TOUR DAY 3: BEANS FIRM, CORN FLAT, HORMUZ TIGHTENS
subheadline: Soybeans hold gains as Cargill lockout ends and tanker traffic at Hormuz slows further; corn goes nowhere on day three of the Pro Farmer tour.
lead: Soybeans closed at $12.11, up 4.5 cents, and finished well off the day's highs after profit-takers hit the afternoon session. Corn sat exactly flat at $4.65. The tour is halfway done, boxed beef is sharply higher, and the Cargill Fort Morgan lockout just ended. Three things changed today. The prices mostly didn't.
the_takeaway: Beans have the news; corn is waiting on scouts. Watch Thursday's tour summary.
teaser: Fort Morgan lockout over, Hormuz tightening, soybeans firm but fading at the highs.

one_number.unit: real Midwest farmland value decline, Q2 2026 year-over-year
one_number.context: The Fed's Seventh District posted its steepest inflation-adjusted farmland value drop since 2016. Strong cash rents are masking the pressure on paper, but asset values moving against producers is a borrowing-power story, not just a balance-sheet footnote.

sections.title: TOUR DAY 3: BEANS LEAD, CORN WAITS
sections.body:
- Soybeans closed at **$12.11**, up 4.5 cents, but the afternoon told you who was driving: profit-takers knocked beans well off session highs after USDA reported a single 136,000-ton sale, a fine number but not a demand statement.
- Corn sat exactly flat at $4.65 for a second straight session; scouts are still in the field and no summary has dropped, so the board has nothing to trade.
- November beans at $12.28 held better than nearby, which says the market is pricing new-crop pod fill, not old-crop demand.
sections.catalyst: USDA reported 136,000 MT soybean sale; Pro Farmer tour ongoing, no summary yet.
sections.bottom_line: Beans have a buyer and a catalyst; corn is in a holding pattern until scouts report.
sections.vs_yesterday: Beans: firmed where corn couldn't follow; tour still the deciding data.

sections.title: FORT MORGAN DEAL DONE; CATTLE FIRM
sections.body:
- The Cargill Fort Morgan lockout ended after five months as Teamsters Local 455 ratified a new five-year contract, closing the chapter on the roughly 6,000 head of daily processing capacity that had been removed since May 19.
- Live cattle at **$224.97** ticked up 0.3%, supported by boxed beef values described as sharply higher in Wednesday's session, a genuine demand signal, not just position noise.
- The screwworm story complicates the reopening math: a new find in Juarez raises the risk that the Aug 24 Douglas, AZ port reopening gets paused if US authorities see increased risk in Sonora or Chihuahua.
sections.catalyst: Cargill Fort Morgan lockout ended; screwworm found in Juarez near reopening date.
sections.bottom_line: Processing capacity comes back, but feeder supply may not if the border reopening slips.
sections.farmer_action: If you are backgrounding feeders targeting fall placement: the Aug 24 port date is now conditional. Watch the Juarez screwworm report before pricing Mexican feeder expectations into your break-even.
sections.vs_yesterday: Cattle: Fort Morgan resolution lands; screwworm in Juarez adds new wrinkle.

sections.title: HORMUZ TIGHTENS AGAIN; CRUDE HOLDS
sections.body:
- WTI held at **$84.99**, up 0.4%, a fourth straight positive session as ship-tracking data showed two Chinese supertankers making U-turns in the Strait of Hormuz, idling rather than transiting, a behavioral signal the market is watching closely on the freight side.
- The Iran-Hormuz situation, which re-escalated in early July with vessels hit and tankers reversing course, has now reached a point where commodity vessel traffic is visibly slowing, adding a supply-chain cost story on top of the price story.
- Diesel tightness remains the actual input-cost pressure for fall fieldwork; crude at $85 is not alarming, but refined fuel shortages and the Iran war's impact on global refining margins are the real number to track.
sections.catalyst: Two Chinese VLCCs made U-turns in Hormuz; tanker traffic slowing per ship-tracking data.
sections.bottom_line: Hormuz is a freight story now as much as a price story; diesel tightness is what hits the field.

outside_the_pit.title: Screwworm Found in Juarez; Aug 24 Port Reopening at Risk
outside_the_pit.body: A new screwworm detection in Juarez, directly across from El Paso, puts the phased reopening of Mexican feeder cattle imports at Douglas, AZ on uncertain footing. If US authorities assess elevated risk in Chihuahua, the border stays closed and the feeder supply tightness that powered this summer's rally extends further.

outside_the_pit.title: Midwest Farmland Values Down 3.7% in Real Terms, Steepest Since 2016
outside_the_pit.body: The Federal Reserve's Seventh District reported inflation-adjusted farmland values fell 3.7% year-over-year in Q2 2026, the sharpest real decline in a decade. Cash rents have held, but producers relying on land equity for operating credit lines are carrying softer collateral into fall loan renewals.

weekly_thread.question: What will Pro Farmer scouts find, and does the tour push December corn above $4.90 or back below $4.75 by Friday?
weekly_thread.status_text: Halfway through the tour with no summary yet; December corn at $4.89 is sitting exactly on the upper threshold, one scout number away from breaking either direction.

the_more_you_know.title: The pod-fill window that sets the bean crop
the_more_you_know.body: With 85% of soybeans in pod-setting stage, the next 10-14 days of overnight lows matter more than daytime highs. Beans set seed weight when nights stay above 55 degrees Fahrenheit; a cold snap now cuts yield faster than a dry week will. That is why the board is watching the 6-10 day outlook, not just soil moisture.

Douglas, AZ feeder cattle port reopening: paused or proceeding depends on USDA screwworm risk assessment in Chihuahua following the Juarez find.
